title: Taxa observed in one or two of five plots cannot pass a strict exact 5% rank test under exchangeability
abstract: We tested a measurement limit for drought and nitrogen community networks with five plots per treatment. We proved that a taxon with positive counts in one or two plots cannot pass an exact absolute-tail rank permutation test at p < 0.05. We checked all 225 nonconstant rank-shape pairs and all 120 plot permutations for each pair. Exact null rejection rates were at most 3.33%. A common approximate t test rejected up to 20% of independent pairs. Sparse occurrence alone can thus change expected edge counts without a change in ecological association. Public experiment documentation supplies the design context. Workbook downloads required authentication, so we did not estimate source treatment effects or reproduce its networks. Exchangeability, average ranks and the strict threshold are necessary assumptions. Regional and temporal biological replication remain untested. The package gives a proof, exhaustive results, an exact pair-test tool, independent checks and source provenance.

display.caption: Exact finite-design results for five paired plots. All values are synthetic rank calculations, not observed treatment effects.
